findings.title: Invite creation has no idempotency contract
findings.why_it_matters: A retry after a lost response, or two near-simultaneous create requests, creates distinct requests and capability links instead of returning the original one. That breaks the documented one-request lifecycle and leaves the owner with extra live links to revoke. Add a client-generated idempotency key to the create request and persist an owner-plus-draft-bound hash with a uniqueness constraint so the service can replay the original invite.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an idempotency_key field to InviteCreateRequest and createLaChungInvite; derive and persist an HMAC/hash over principal_id, idempotency key, and normalized draft in LaChungRequestRow with a unique constraint. On conflict, return the existing still-valid invite/token envelope after verifying the draft matches; add lost-response and concurrent-create tests.

findings.title: Recipient labels persist without encryption
findings.why_it_matters: A recipient’s chosen name or nickname is personal social data and is stored directly in the database, so a database read exposes it without the scoped envelope key required by the product contract. The capability token is encrypted, but the label is not. Store the normalized label in a record-bound envelope ciphertext and decrypt it only in owner-authorized or valid-capability projections, with a migration/backfill for existing rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace LaChungRequestRow.recipient_label with recipient_label_ciphertext (and key-version metadata if required by the existing envelope format), encrypt/decrypt it with a request-bound context in LaChungService, and add a key-aware migration/backfill plus owner/public projection tests.
evidence: AGENTS.md:22-25 -- "Inventory every personal-data field ... stored" and "Verify ... encryption ..."; runtime behavior and privacy documentation must remain consistent.

findings.title: Invite creation and resend bypass admission limits
findings.why_it_matters: An authenticated owner can create or resend unlimited active capability links because the admission middleware only covers guest creation, birth computation, and public routes. This leaves the documented create/resend abuse control unenforced and permits capability-link spam from a single session. Add owner invite creation and resend paths to the admission policy with limits appropriate for the seven-day lifecycle.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend _policy with explicit POST policies for /v1/la-chung/requests and /v1/la-chung/requests/{request_id}/resend (using a route-aware match), then add tests that the limits return 429 without affecting revoke or valid public submit flows.

AGENTS.md:16 -- "Review ... abuse/rate limits ... public endpoints, share links ..."

findings.title: Public invite API omits no-index header
findings.why_it_matters: The public capability API can expose the recipient label and curated response prompt at a token-bearing URL, but its defense-in-depth headers do not prohibit indexing. Static frontend headers cover the shared page, not direct API responses. Add the same X-Robots-Tag policy used by public share artifacts to keep every public invite surface consistently non-indexable.
findings.suggested_fix: Set response.headers["X-Robots-Tag"] = "noindex, nofollow, noarchive" in _safe_public and extend the public invite header tests to cover successful and terminal responses.
evidence: apps/api/app/api/v1/routes/la_chung.py:92-98 -- _safe_public sets Cache-Control, Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, and Content-Security-Policy, but no X-Robots-Tag header.
AGENTS.md:30 -- "Treat every public share/invite as sensitive-by-capability: prevent caching/indexing, keep tokens out of logs/referrers, and preserve revocation behavior."

residual_risks: The chart-synthesis runbook marks distributed edge limits, capability URL redaction in CDN/WAF/proxy logs, native device validation, and store disclosures as release No-Go evidence. They cannot be confirmed from this working copy alone.
testing_gaps: No test was found that proves create-invite replay returns the original capability for an identical idempotency key after a lost response or concurrent requests.
No test was found that verifies recipient labels are encrypted at rest or that the public invite API emits a no-index response header.
